# Five objections, answered

## 1. "I can read the Markdown. Why would I pay for text files?"

You can. The graded eval suite ships with it, so you can read the cases and
the answer keys and see how it is judged. What you are paying for is not secrecy, it is the work: the evidence
rubric that stops ten compliments counting as validation, nine modules of
questions, 21 test scenarios with answer keys, and the
updates when something is found to be wrong.

The free version is still MIT-licensed and still free. If it is enough, use
it. Nobody is stopping you, and no licence key here pretends otherwise.

## 2. "ChatGPT or Claude will do this for free."

They will, and they will tell you your idea is promising. That is the
difference. Ask a general model about your startup and it will invent a market
size, agree with your premise, and produce the deck you asked for. This one
scores your evidence first and refuses the deck when the evidence is not
there.

The free alternative is not a worse version of this. It is the opposite
behaviour.

## 3. "I already bought a validation report."

A report is a one-shot document about an idea you had last month. This is a
conversation that remembers what you tested and what happened, opens on your
unrun test, and writes down the verdicts it got wrong so it gets sharper.

Those reports are priced per idea. This is unlimited use on every idea you
have, and it is the same price whether you validate one or twenty.

(No price comparison is quoted here on purpose. Every figure this product puts
in front of a founder carries a source or an UNVERIFIED marker, and the sales
copy is held to the same rule.)

## 4. "It will just tell me to talk to more customers."

With a score of 0, yes — because that is the honest answer, and it says so in
one of four words rather than a paragraph of encouragement. Bring evidence and
the answer changes. In testing, a founder with 14 interviews and 4 paying
workarounds was told the problem was settled and the gap was the business
model, in the same turn.

## 5. "I'm not technical. Will I be able to use it?"

Nothing to run. Upload one file in the Claude app, or copy a folder. No
account, no API key, no database. The build advice assumes you do not write
code — it recommends prompt-to-app tools and ships ready-to-paste prompts, and
payments are a hosted checkout link with no payment code at all.
